A real look inside QikCal

Small food logs.
A clearer week.

Follow the everyday loop: log a meal, find a food in the offline USDA catalogue, save meals you repeat, then look back at your week.

This silent preview uses real iPhone Simulator screens with sample diary entries. Calorie values are estimates from USDA FoodData Central.

A little structure, none of the fuss

Food logging that fits between everything else.

QikCal keeps the everyday loop short: choose what you ate, adjust it to your plate, and get back to your day.

A

Find your food

Search the bundled USDA FoodData Central catalogue, or add a food yourself when you need a simple personal entry.

B

Make the portion yours

Choose a reported serving or enter grams. Calories and available nutrients scale with the amount you log.

C

Look back, gently

See your seven-day pattern, edit a log, or share a recap when you choose. Nothing is posted for you.

Your diary stays yours

Private by design. Useful offline.

Your diary is stored on your iPhone. QikCal has no account, advertising SDK, analytics SDK or server diary. Your food log is excluded from device backups, and you can export or delete it in Settings.

Food energy is an estimate from reference data. Values can be missing or vary by food and preparation; QikCal is a diary, not medical advice.

The bundled catalogue contains 13,649 food records from USDA FoodData Central. The data is public domain; attribution is provided in the app.
